chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is written in the Torah: 'O son of Adam! Free yourself for My worship, I shall fill your heart with riches and will not fatigue you to your seeking, and it would be upon Me to aim to excel you and fill your heart with fear from Me, and that if you don’t free yourself for My worship, I shall fill your heart with a pre-occupation with the world, then I will not excel you and will exhaust you to the seeking (of the livelihood)'.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between worship and provision in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt, highlights the Shia theological concept of 'Tafarrugh' (spiritual concentration) as the key to divine provision (Rizq). It illustrates the reciprocal relationship between devotion and sustenance, where prioritizing worship ensures God covers one's needs, while neglecting it leads to being consumed by worldly distractions and self-reliance.
